overview: This Senate resolution recognizes April 2025 as "Community College Month" to celebrate the more than 1,000 community colleges across the United States. It notes the history of community colleges, starting with the first public one in Illinois in 1901, and their role today in offering affordable college classes, job training, and dual enrollment for high school students. It describes the many working adults, parents, veterans, and first-generation students they serve. The resolution is a statement of recognition and does not create programs or provide money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 5, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution rightly highlights community colleges as affordable, local institutions that train workers and open doors to higher education.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding to community colleges.
